Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for Omega Squared

Source: R/ss_aipe_omega_squared_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_omega_squared_sensitivity.Rd

Quantifies how much misspecification of the population \(\omega^2\) distorts an AIPE-based sample size plan. The planner ss_aipe_omega_squared solves for the smallest N that yields an expected CI width below the target at the planning value. Here we generate G datasets from a balanced one-way ANOVA with population \(\omega^2 = \)true_omega_squared and df_effect + 1 groups at the planner-recommended N, compute the noncentral F confidence interval on each replication via ci_omega_squared, and summarize the realized widths and coverage of true_omega_squared.

Usage

ss_aipe_omega_squared_sensitivity(
  true_omega_squared = NULL,
  supposed_omega_squared = NULL,
  df_effect,
  width,
  specified_N = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_omega_squared

Population \(\omega^2\) (the data generating value); in \([0, 1)\).

supposed_omega_squared

The supposed \(\omega^2\), the planning value from which ss_aipe_omega_squared plans the study (not an estimate computed from data); supply this or specified_N but not both.

df_effect

Numerator degrees of freedom for the omnibus F, equal to the number of groups minus 1.

width

Desired full width of the confidence interval on \(\omega^2\).

specified_N

Total sample size to evaluate (incompatible with supposed_omega_squared).

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

assurance

Optional assurance probability passed to ss_aipe_omega_squared when resolving the planned sample size.

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications (default 1000).

print_iter

Logical. Print iteration index per replication.

filename

Optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the sample \(\hat\omega^2\), the two confidence limits, the interval width, and two indicators of whether the interval missed true_omega_squared below or above): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with rows for mean / median / SD of the realized \(\hat\omega^2\) and interval width, the proportion of intervals at or below width, tail-specific and overall empirical non-coverage of true_omega_squared, and the input echoes, including assurance (present only when an assurance was supplied).

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Kelley, K. (2007). Confidence intervals for standardized effect sizes: Theory, application, and implementation. Journal of Statistical Software, 20(8), 1–24. doi:10.18637/jss.v020.i08

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapter 3 on effect size measures.)

See also

ss_aipe_omega_squared, ci_omega_squared

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Examples

# Well-specified: planner used omega^2 = 0.10, truth is 0.10.
# G is kept small here so the example runs quickly; raise it for a
# stable sensitivity estimate.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_omega_squared_sensitivity(
  true_omega_squared     = 0.10,
  supposed_omega_squared = 0.10,
  df_effect = 2, width = 0.10,
  G = 25, print_iter = FALSE
)
#> During the iterative sample size search, the noncentral F lower-limit clamp in ci_nc_F() fired in 10 intermediate evaluations.
#>  term                   value
#>  mean_omega_squared     0.067
#>  median_omega_squared   0.070
#>  sd_omega_squared       0.020
#>  mean_ci_width          0.085
#>  median_ci_width        0.088
#>  sd_ci_width            0.010
#>  pct_ci_less_width      0.920
#>  pct_ci_miss_low        0.000
#>  pct_ci_miss_high       0.320
#>  total_type_I_error     0.320
#>  total_N                471  
#>  n_per_group            157  
#>  true_omega_squared     0.100
#>  supposed_omega_squared 0.100
#>  width                  0.100
#>  conf_level             0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 25
#>
